Progressive intracranial arterial stenosis; cerebral infarction or hemorrhage causes brain injury in more than 30% over the symptomatic course.
Branchial and ear malformation syndrome with sensorineural hearing loss; lacrimal stenosis lacks evidence of frequency sufficient for inclusion.
Progressive myoclonic epilepsy; scoliosis in 2/2 and generalized amyotrophy in 1/2 support musculoskeletal involvement, although reported numbers are small.
A developmental disorder of speech production falls within the neurodevelopmental axis.
Central/autonomic dysfunction; achalasia and intestinal dysmotility in 3/3; scoliosis/kyphosis in 1/3. Hypoventilation reflects central control failure.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the brainstem.
GPI biosynthesis disorder with severe encephalopathy; scoliosis in 5/5 and strabismus in 5/5 support skeletal and ocular involvement; optic atrophy only 1/5.
Reproductive system neoplasms have no applicable axis across the umbrella; endocrine involvement is confined to particular subtypes.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by epiphyseal stippling and tibial/metacarpal shortening; no established metabolic disorder or other common organ damage.
Hair follicle tumor of the scalp with local skin ulceration and tissue destruction.
Hereditary prostate cancer affects a reproductive organ outside the specified axes.
Inherited distal skeletal muscle disease; cardiac and respiratory involvement vary by subtype and are not established across most of the umbrella.

Congenital unilateral absence or hypoplasia of the humerus.
Malignancy of an undescended testis is reproductive; endocrine dysfunction is not inherent to this tumor concept.
Focal epilepsy syndrome defined by cerebral seizure activity.
Degeneration of the basal ganglia causes regression and movement dysfunction; dysphagia is neurologic, and recurrent infections are separate conditions.
Innate immune deficiency of the lectin complement pathway; associated infections do not establish common intrinsic damage to another organ.
SCN1B-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; no evidence of common independent organ damage beyond the nervous system.
Immune-mediated inflammation after immune restoration; affected organs vary with the antigen, without a single additional organ qualifying across the syndrome.
Congenital absence of the corpus callosum; extra-neurologic damage is not established as common across isolated and syndromic cases.
Outer retinal dysfunction causes visual field loss; proposed infectious or autoimmune causes remain unproven and do not establish an immune mechanism label.
Adenoma arising in the intrahepatic bile ducts; biliary tissue belongs to the hepatic axis.
